quarterly_data.quarter: TTM Technologies Jefferies Global Industrials Conference 2026 (09-09-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: THE SHAPE OF THE DATA-CENTER CUSTOMER BASE (CEO Edwin Roks): TTM will not name customers - 'we cannot disclose our customers. We have very strict NDAs with them. But these are the big guys. These are the big guys you read in the newspaper every day, correct? 10, 15 of these big customers, and then a tail of another 50. Which is helping us to understand the landscape, to understand what are the trends.' On hyperscaler roadmap alignment: 'the first thing what we do is align with our customers, and these are the multiple hyperscalers. We also like to show, let's say, demonstrators. I hate to go with only PowerPoints to our customers... So alignment with these hyperscalers, by the way, with all our customers, is going very well.' Management also framed N+M as the start of a technology curve rather than a one-off: 'where you do N+M, which is a new technology, only the first generation of that new technology trend, is working out very well. We're ramping up.'
quarterly_data.figure: 10, 15 of these big customers, and then a tail of another 50

quarterly_data.quarter: TTM Technologies Jefferies Global Industrials Conference 2026 (09-09-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: DATA CENTER AND NETWORKING IS SET TO OUTGROW DEFENSE INTO THE MIX (CEO): asked about the long-term split of the ~80% of the business tied to AI and aerospace/defense, which is roughly even today, 'If you look at how fast data centers and networking is growing right now, it will likely get aerospace and defense to a 30% portion. Now it's 40%. But who cares, because the business is growing nicely in double digits, and it is very sustainable.' The strategic direction is away from a pure PCB identity: 'we are indeed coming from a traditional PCB company, but we have to find another word for PCB... We're moving into, let's say, a more, I would say, communication and sensing company' - built on heterogeneous, very compact packaging and then modules, subsystems and systems, plus geographic expansion into Europe where management expects to do more acquisitions. The CEO's framing of the AI role: with Moore's law slowing, 'What we provide is, let's say, combining these chips. That's why we like to call ourselves the nervous system... combining these chips in a very efficient way with low latency and high bandwidth.'
quarterly_data.figure: data center and networking growth likely takes aerospace and defense to a 30% portion from 40% today

quarterly_data.quarter: TTM Technologies Jefferies Global Industrials Conference 2026 (09-09-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: COPPER AND GLASS ARE THE TWO WATCHED INPUTS - NO ISSUES YET (CEO): asked about supply-chain constraints that could temper delivery, 'We are focused every day, every hour on the supply chain... this is almost a full-time job of our COO. We follow, let's say, what's happening with copper. We follow what's happening with glass and making sure that we don't get tied here. So far so good. We are very transparent to our customers also.' The mitigations named were multiple qualified suppliers and TTM's position at the top of the technology stack: 'The good thing is that these suppliers also focus more on the high-end, and that's exactly where we play. We don't see issues right now, but absolutely it's our focus every day.'

quarterly_data.quarter: TTM Technologies Jefferies Global Industrials Conference 2026 (09-09-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: CAPACITY IS ADDED IN SMALL BROWNFIELD STEPS AND IS NOT EXPECTED TO CONSTRAIN GROWTH (CEO and Cathy Gridley, President of Aerospace and Defense): 'we do it in a more, I would say, in a disciplined way. When we see growth... we do a $50 million investment here and $100 million there. You don't see us a lot in, although we did it... with Syracuse, and we have examples with Penang in Malaysia, where we did greenfield, but we love brownfield. We love, let's say, a building which is next door, which we can use... and now we put all these drill stations... We can follow the demand cycle very carefully.' On the defense side: 'in North America, in the U.S., we have 16 facilities that are dedicated or largely dedicated to defense... We have to add pieces of equipment to expand the capacity within that footprint, but it's a measured approach. Capacity is not going to be a constraint for us.' The Syracuse Ultra-HDI plant was a true greenfield next to the 2018 Anaren facility and went 'from greenfield and within 23 months, I handed the keys over to operations so that they could go into production'; UHDI itself 'is not a new technology. It's been built in Asia for quite a long time... What is new is the application of that capability in defense and defense systems, and that has to be done here in the U.S.'
quarterly_data.figure: a $50 million investment here and $100 million there; 16 facilities dedicated or largely dedicated to defense; Syracuse greenfield to production within 23 months

quarterly_data.quarter: TTM Technologies Jefferies Global Industrials Conference 2026 (09-09-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: A THIRD ACQUISITION IN 2026 - EPIQ SOLUTIONS (CEO and Cathy Gridley): alongside the Swiss Technology Group and ILFA deals, management discussed 'the recent acquisition of Epiq, which is a very nice one', adding that European expansion 'will not end there'. Epiq 'brings to us a very modern, very cutting-edge, forward-leaning capability in software-defined radios and strong comms capability and brings us additional RF spectrum capability, which when married with our preexisting RF, gives us the full spectrum of RF capability for our customers', modernising the communications capability acquired with Telephonics in 2022; it had been on TTM's watch list since Veritas acquired it in 2022. Management signalled more of the same: 'What you will see is more acquisitions in Europe... We will do more on the communication and sensing side.'
